extracted.intended_audience: ACUS members and staff, consultants, committee members, and others preparing or studying ACUS recommendations
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural steps and documentary expectations for producing an Administrative Conference of the United States (ACUS) Recommendation or Statement, from project initiation through Assembly adoption and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory function — bringing public and private sectors together
rubrics_metrics.description: The main statutory function of ACUS is to bring together the public and private sectors to recommend improvements to administrative and regulatory processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This frames ACUS's purpose and the audience/stakeholder engagement expected as part of its work; it signals that recommendations should aim at improving administrative/regulatory processes and involve both public and private sector perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project initiation — Office of the Chairman engages consultants with Council approval
rubrics_metrics.description: ACUS’s Office of the Chairman, with the approval of the Council, engages consultants to study administrative processes or procedures that may need improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement of consultants requires Council approval and is used to identify processes or procedures that may need improvement; this is the formal trigger for a study that can lead to recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research report — comprehensive report proposing recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultants or in-house staff then prepare a comprehensive research report proposing recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The output of the study phase is a comprehensive research report which must propose concrete recommendations; the report is the substantive basis for subsequent committee review and drafting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee deliberation — discussion and draft Recommendation preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: An ACUS committee discusses this report, preparing a draft Recommendation to submit to the Council and, with approval, to the Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee discussion is the forum for transforming the research report into a formal draft Recommendation; the draft must be suitable for Council consideration and potential Assembly review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval and adoption — Council approval, Assembly debate, and final adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: Following a debate the Assembly adopts the final Recommendation, which ACUS undertakes to implement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The process requires Council approval to move to the Assembly; the Assembly debates the draft and, if adopted, the Recommendation becomes final and subject to ACUS implementation efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements — alternative, less-formal outputs from the same process
rubrics_metrics.description: On occasion, the ACUS membership has acted to adopt a 'Statement' to express its views on a particular matter without making a formal recommendation on the subject. Statements are typically the product of the same process that leads to recommendations, but may set forth issues, conclusions from a study, or comments, rather than recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements serve as an alternative outcome when the body wishes to express views, issues, conclusions, or comments instead of formal recommendations; ACUS has adopted 19 such statements included in the searchable database of recommendations.
